subject: Clarify SOC 2 coverage window and next reissue process

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@novaretail.com>

Date: Fri, May 28, 2026 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Request — latest SOC 2 + coverage clarification

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you’re well. Our procurement/security team is preparing NovaRetail’s vendor review for Q2 renewals and I ran into a coverage question on the SOC 2 materials we have on file. We currently have:
- SOC2_TypeII_2024-10-31.pdf (covers through 10/31/2024)
- SOC2_Bridge_2025-05-01.pdf (dated 05/01/2025)

Procurement is flagging the bridge as "expired" and says they need either a reissued Type II that covers the rollover period or a bridge that explicitly extends to a date after the procurement review window (they prefer a signed bridge through at least 06/15/2026). Can you confirm:
1) Whether Redwood has a newly reissued SOC 2 Type II that supersedes the 10/31/2024 report and, if so, the audit coverage window on that document;
2) Whether the bridge we have on file is still valid or can be extended;
3) If there are any scope changes (new services, subservice providers, or infrastructure changes) between the 10/31/2024 report and any reissue that we should be aware of.

If a reissue is pending, please let us know an ETA and whether you can provide a signed letter we can share with procurement in the interim. We need to close this by early June to avoid delaying a renewal.

Thanks — appreciate the quick help.

Best,
Priya Desai
Vendor Risk Manager
NovaRetail Inc.

Hi Priya — thanks for the note and good catch. Short answers up front: we do not yet have a fully signed reissued Type II in your portal; the bridge you have is valid but it is narrow in scope which is what's creating the procurement flag. Details below and next steps.

What happened: our last fully issued SOC 2 Type II covers 11/01/2023–10/31/2024 (file you referenced). We initiated the next audit cycle in Q1 2026. The audit firm completed fieldwork in late May and provided an initial reissue package; final auditor signatures are pending (they're doing the limited partner sign-off). Because the auditor final signature is outstanding, we have not published a fully executed Type II to customers yet.

Bridge letter status: the bridge dated 05/01/2025 was issued as a short-form attestation to cover the immediate gap; however, procurement teams vary in how they accept bridge letters — some treat the 05/01/2025 date as "not forward-looking enough." We can request an auditor-provided extension/endorsement that explicitly extends coverage through 06/15/2026 if procurement needs that.

Scope notes: there are no material scope removals. We added a new EU region (aws-eu-west-1) for Dedicated customers in early 2025 but that region is not in-scope for the US-only controls tested in the current audit cycle. The Dedicated product (reserved capacity) and hosted API were included in scope for technical controls — no changes to the set of subservice providers other than routine cloud provider region additions.

Proposed plan (quick timeline):
- Today: I’ll open a formal reissue request with our auditor and ask for either
  a) a signed reissue to be finalized by 2026-06-10, or
  b) an interim auditor extension/endorsement that explicitly extends the bridge to 06/15/2026 if full reissue timing slips.
- By Monday: I will share a cover note and the bridge PDF that you can give to procurement, and include a simple one-paragraph coverage summary you can paste into the vendor packet.
- If your procurement requires DocuSign on a reissue plan/agreement, we can route a short agreement for signature (I’ve looped in Dylan from Legal to assist).

I’ll follow up with the documents in the next message; copying Dylan and Hannah so they can jump in on the legal/audit details.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
